item.content:encoded:
Friday was a big day for the Minnesota Twins. They executed a trade with the Los Angeles Dodgers to move the Twins’ former No. 1 overall pick, Royce Lewis. In return, Minnesota acquired right-handed pitcher Bobby Miller and catching prospect Francisco Espinoza.
Of course, the trade officially ended Lewis’ tenure with the Twins but it also raised questions about what the team’s plans were for Miller.
Miller was once considered one of baseball’s most promising young starting pitchers. He is now 27 years old, and injuries, along with inconsistent performances, have completely changed his journey to the majors.
Minnesota may have an entirely different path for Miller to take to find his way to the mound. Relief pitching.
That possibility makes the trade make a lot more sense.
Bobby Miller Has Struggled
The Dodgers used their first-round selection of the 2020 MLB Draft to pick up Miller. He was a standout from the beginning and worked his way to being one of the organization’s top pitching prospects.
He even debuted at the MLB level in 2023 and gave the team plenty of reasons for optimism. He finished his rookie season with an 11-4 record, a 3.76 ERA, and 119 strikeouts across 124 1/3 innings.
The tools were there, and he looked like he was going to be a dependable member of the Los Angeles rotation. That was not the case.
His early success seemed to be hard to replicate. Over the next three seasons, he made just 18 MLB appearances, in which he recorded an 8.30 ERA over 68 1/3 innings.
To make matters worse, his struggles continued at the minor league level.
Then, injuries happened. He dealt with right shoulder inflammation in 2024 and missed almost the entire 2026 season because of more shoulder issues. Last season, he only played in three Major League games and threw only 7 1/3 innings.
Twins Give Miller Another Opportunity
It is possible that the Twins have a different plan for Miller. The organization already added starting pitcher Sonny Grey to the staff and have several competing for roles on the rotation.
That’s what makes a bullpen assignment make a lot more sense for Miller.
Miller already has experience as both a starter and a reliever. Giving him a chance to have shorter outings could let him get his confidence back using his best pitches.
But, it won’t solve all his problems. Command still remains a problem, and his shoulder is going to have to prove its durability.
Relief pitchers have to control walks to avoid getting into difficult situations. Minnesota will have to see marked improvement before Miller can be tagged as a dependable late-inning option.
Miller still has a minor league option remaining which gives Minnesota some flexibility if he needs to develop or ramp up his innings before joining the Majors.
Spring Training will be an interesting time for Miller as he is evaluated for a spot on the team. There is no guarantee to any player at any time, and there sure isn’t with Miller.
Minnesota doesn’t need Miller to be a starting pitcher for the trade to be valuable. If he can just develop into an effective reliever, he will be valuable to a team that needs to improve its bullpen, and he will have restarted his career.
Laura Lambert resides in Wiggins, Colo. With her husband, Ricky and two sons, Brayden and Boedy. She attended the University of Northern Colorado while studying economics. She is an accomplished rodeo athlete and barrel horse trainer. Over the years, Laura has been active in journalism in a variety of roles. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers received a message from right-handed pitcher Bobby Miller after he was surprisingly traded to the Minnesota Twins as part of the deal to land former No. 1 overall pick Royce Lewis. He sent a message to the team, his former teammates and fans on his personal Instagram account
"Forever grateful for the opportunity to wear Dodger blue," Miller wrote. "From the moment I was drafted in 2020, the Dodgers organization took me in as a young kid with a dream and gave me the opportunity to live it. Los Angeles became home, and the people I met along the way became family. I’ll forever cherish the memories, relationships, and experiences that came with being a Dodger. To the entire Dodgers organization, my teammates, coaches, staff, and especially the fans, thank you for believing in me, supporting me, and making these years so special."
In other news, there is an update on a contract extension for the Dodgers' center fielder of the future, Andy Pages. The soon-to-be 26-year-old posted another promising season in 2026, his first as an All-Star, and even received the first MVP votes of his career.
Given his elite status as a defender, his arm strength that puts him on the next level as well as his consistent bat, his price will likely only rise if he keeps things up.
Finally, Dodgers fans were called out by Milwaukee Brewers infielder Cooper Pratt. He compared the postseason atmosphere to that of the San Diego Padres at Petco Park while making an appearances on the Baseball Is Dead Podcast.
"When we played the Dodgers, it just kind of felt like a regular season game. When we went to San Diego, it was so loud. They would throw a strike, and everyone was screaming. It was a little different in LA," Pratt said. "Not that they weren't loud — because when they got loud, they got loud. Because those speakers in center field are loud. But it just didn't feel like San Diego or Tampa Bay."

item.content:encoded:
ドジャース、大丈夫か？
現地2026年11月20日、ノンテンダー・デッドライン（Non-Tender Deadline）を迎えたMLBで、ロサンゼルス・ドジャースとミネソタ・ツインズの間で非常に興味深いトレードが成立しました。
かつての「全体1位」と「トッププロスペクト右腕」が動く、ロマンと再起を懸けたディールとなっています。早速、トレードの詳細と両クラブの思惑を整理していきたいと思います。
それにしてもドジャースは大丈夫でしょうかね？このかつての「全体1位」は怪我のオンパレードでまともにフルシーズンを戦えたことがないのですが・・・。
トレード詳細
このトレードは3選手が動く1対2のトレードです。今回のトレードで動く選手は以下の通りです。年齢はシーズン半分の2027年7月1日時点の年齢で記載しています。
ドジャース獲得
- ロイス・ルイス（Royce Lewis / 28）INF | B/T: R/R
ツインズ獲得：
- ボビー・ミラー（Bobby Miller/28）RHP
- フランシスコ・エスピノーザ（Francisco Espinoza/20) C| B/T: R/R
選手プロフィール＆2026年シーズンの成績
ロイス・ルイス（ドジャースへ）
- Date of Birth： 1999年6月5日
- ドラフト： 2017年 ツインズ1巡目（全体1位）
- 2026年成績（MIN）： 125試合、BA.227、OBP.287、SLG.380、OPS.667（OPS+ 86）、HR 15、RBI 57、SB 16
ロイス・ルイスはカリフォルニア州出身で、2017年ドラフト全体1位としてツインズに入団。2023年にはわずか58試合の出場ながら、HR 15、OPS.921（wRC+ 152）をマークし、ポストシーズンでも大活躍してツインズのポストシーズン連敗記録のストップに貢献しました。
しかし、キャリアを通じて膝や腹斜筋、ハムストリングなどの故障に悩まされ続けており、ここ2シーズン（2025年・2026年）も思うような打撃成績を残せていません。今季5月にはマイナー降格も経験しています。
ボビー・ミラー（ツインズへ）
- Date of Birth： 1999年4月5日
- ドラフト： 2020年 ドジャース1巡目（全体29位）
- 2026年成績（LAD）： 3試合、0勝0敗、ERA 3.68、7.1IP 、SO 8、WHIP 1.23
4シームのアベレージが97mph誇るボビー・ミラーは2020年のドジャースのドラフト1巡目指名右腕。ルーキーイヤーとなった2023年には22先発で11勝4敗、ERA 3.76とローテーションの柱として大ブレイクしましたが、2024年以降は右肩の故障や制球難に苦しみ、2026年は開幕からILに入り、9月にブルペン要員としてようやくメジャー復帰を果たしたばかりでした。
フランシスコ・エスピノーザ（ツインズへ）
- Date of Birth：2007年3月16日
- 出身：ベネズエラ （2024年1月15日、インターナショナル・アマチュア・FAとしてドジャースとマイナー契約。
- プレー：このベネズエラ出身の若手捕手はプロ初年度の2024年は17歳でドミニカン・サマー・リーグでプレー。2025年はACLドジャースに所属し、35試合に出場して打率.350を記録。2026年は、アリゾナ・コンプレックス・リーグと、カリフォルニア・リーグ（クラスA）のオンタリオ・タワー・バザーズの計2チームで合計46試合に出場。打撃成績はBA .317、OBP .411、SLG.422で、HR 3、RBi 25を記録。守備面では2026年のCS%は12%（結構走られました）。
- クラブ内トップ30プロスペクト圏外ながら、クラスAでコンタクト能力と出塁率をアピールした楽しみな素材です。
背景
ドジャースの狙い：M・ロハス引退の穴埋め
ドジャースは今オフ、2026年シーズン限りで現役を引退したベテランINF，ミゲル・ロハス（Miguel Rojas）の穴を埋める右打ちのユーティリティ内野手を探していました。まあ、ミゲル・ロハスの守備はミスター球際でしたね！！
地元カリフォルニア出身のロイス・ルイスは、3B・2B・1Bを守れる柔軟性を持ち、マックス・マンシーのバックアップやプラトゥーン要員としてもフィットしています。ロイス・ルイスの力は本物ではあるのですが、但し、上述のようにロイス・ルイスはいかせん、怪我が多いのです。
ロイス・ルイスに怪我が無ければ、ドジャースにとってこのトレードは大成功ということに。果たしてチームドクターも巻き込んでドジャースがこのロイス・ルイスの体とうまく付き合って行けるのか、注目ポイントでもあります。
ツインズの狙い：ペイロール削減と若返り
一方のツインズは、同日にベイリー・オーバー、トレバー・ラーナック、マット・ウォールナーをノンテンダー（FA）とするなど、大規模なロースター整理と年俸削減（サラリーダンプ）を断行しました。
調停2年目のロイス・ルイスは、2027年シーズンのサラリーが$5.1Mドルと予想されており、実はツインズにとってはかつての全体1位もノンテンダー候補の一人でした。
1Bにはコディー・クレメンス、3Bにはブルックス・リーといった若手・中堅の台頭もあり、ロイス・ルイスをそのまま放出する代わりに「かつての剛腕のミラー（マイナーオプションあり）」と「プロスペクトの19歳捕手エスピノーザ」の2名を獲得できたのは、非常に現実的で巧みな立ち回りと言えます。
環境の変化が吉と出るか
このトレードは2023年時点であればMLB代表する若手スター同士の超大型トレードになっていたはず。互いに怪我と不振でキャリアの岐路に立たされる中、環境を変えることで再び輝きを取り戻すことができるのか、2027年シーズンの大きな注目ポイントになりそうです。
ロイス・ルイス獲得でドジャースは阪神・佐藤をどうする？
今回のトレードで気になるのは阪神からポスティング申請でMLB入りを目指している佐藤輝明選手の動向。ドジャースも有力な候補先と見られる中、どう動くのでしょうか？
ドジャースは今季終盤は大谷選手の不調もあり、打線がまるで爆発力を欠いてしまいましたが、それでもマックス・マンシーがいたことでなんとかNLCSまで進むことが出来たと言っていいでしょう。
ドジャースとマックス・マンシーの契約は2026年2月にサインした1年/$10M (2027) + 2028 10Mクラブオプション（$3Mバイアウト）で延長契約済み。
怪我の多いロイス・ルイスがどこまで機能するか？にも依るのですが、仮にドジャースが佐藤選手を獲得した場合、マックス・マンシーもしますし、守備はOFが優先されそうに思います。
果たして、このディールが佐藤選手の動向に何か影響を与えたのか？ここも後日に答え合わせがでそうですね。
お読みいただき、ありがとうございました。

item.content:encoded:
Teoscar Hernández has been a driving force behind the heartbeat of the Dodgers over the last three seasons, and he was affectionately given the moniker "Mr. Seeds" by the fanbase.
After an All-Star campaign in 2024, injuries have slowed down the former 30-homer threat from getting back to that pedigree. Paired with his questionable defense in the corner outfield positions and with just one year left on his current contract, Hernández's time in Los Angeles may have very well run out, especially with the 21-year-old Josue De Paula waiting to emerge in the distance.
Sonja Chen of MLB.com lists out the pros and cons of a potential Hernández deal and the pros and cons on if the Dodgers stand pat. One major downside to shipping off the 2024 Home Run Derby champion, Chen notes, is losing yet another integral piece of the locker room the last three years, considering Miguel Rojas's retirement and the uncertainty of Kiké Hernández returning for 2027.
If the Dodgers were to trade Hernández, then they would lose a veteran righty bat on a team that can skew left-handed at times. But while his impact on the lineup is noteworthy, his impact on his teammates may be more important. Hernández is a leader in a L.A. clubhouse that has already lost Miguel Rojas to retirement and Kiké Hernández to free agency this offseason. Preserving team chemistry may be more of an art than a science, but it has to be something the Dodgers weigh carefully as they build out their roster for next season.
If you, the reader, are a habitual viewer of Dodger baseball, then you may have noticed an abundance of New Balance commercials featuring Shohei Ohtani, with Kool & The Gang's "Hollywood Swinging" playing in the background. Ohtani's time as one of the many faces of New Balance won't be coming to an end anytime soon, as he signed a lifetime deal with the company on Friday which includes a research lab under his namesake. Steve Henson at the Los Angeles Times has more.
The Dodgers didn't waste much time looking for a replacement for the now-retired Miguel Rojas, as they swung a deal for Minnesota Twins infielder and southern California native Royce Lewis in exchange for former-top prospect Bobby Miller and catcher Francisco Espinoza.
Andy McCullough of The Athletic gives the Dodgers a B grade in the deal, highlighting the upside that the former no. 1 overall pick had shown in years prior despite the numerous injuries that have plagued his career so far.
I dig this move for the Dodgers. The team wanted to fortify its infield depth, especially if they are parting ways with utilityman Kiké Hernández. Lewis has played all over the infield. The team wanted to get younger. Among the Dodgers' regulars, the 27-year-old Lewis is older than only 25-year-old Andy Pages. He has power and can still generate elite bat speed. Maybe the Dodgers can unlock something.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers' trade for infielder Royce Lewis and decision not to non-tender outfielder Alex Call were the stories of Friday's deadline.
Call has been a candidate to be off the Dodgers roster since the trade deadline. However, he's continued to remain with the club.
Another player was non-tendered before Friday's deadline, though.
The Dodgers non-tendered right-handed pitcher Jake Cousins, who was a candidate for arbitration before he was designated for assignment earlier this week when the Dodgers added four prospects to their 40-man roster. Now, Cousins is officially a free agent after being non-tendered.
Jake Cousins Dodgers Tenure
Cousins, 32, joined the Dodgers last offseason on a one-year deal that paid him $950,000. He spent most of the season recovering from Tommy John surgery he underwent in June 2025. In September, he played in some rehab games for the Triple-A Oklahoma City Comets.
Across six games, Cousins allowed five runs over 4.1 innings for a 10.38 ERA. He had five walks to four strikeouts and allowed four hits.
Jake Cousins MLB Career
Cousins was initially drafted by the Washington Nationals in the 20th round of the 2017 draft.
He was released ahead of the 2019 season and went to the independent Frontier League. Then, midway through the 2019 season, the Milwaukee Brewers purchased his contract.
Cousins made his MLB debut with the Brewers in 2021, finishing with a 2.70 ERA across 30 innings. He then again had a 2.70 ERA in 2022 across 13.1 innings, but dealt with an elbow injury for much of the year.
Since 2023, Cousins has bounced around with the Brewers, Houston Astros, Chicago White Sox and New York Yankees organizations. In 2024, he made 37 appearances for the Yankees, finishing with a 2.37 ERA and 53 strikeouts over 38 innings.
The right-hander opened the 2025 season on the injured list with an elbow injury. He ended up undergoing Tommy John surgery, and has been working his way back ever since.
Cousins should be ready for the start of the 2027 season, and thus could have a market for a major league deal this offseason. If not, he could sign a minor league deal with an invitation to spring training, and then look to work his way onto a team's Opening Day roster.
Who Did the Dodgers Tender a Contract To?
In addition to avoiding arbitration with Call, the Dodgers tendered contracts to four players: outfielder Andy Pages and right-handed pitchers Brock Stewart, Emmet Sheehan and Gavin Stone.
The team also traded for infielder Royce Lewis from the Minnesota Twins in exchange for right-handed pitcher Bobby Miller and catching prospect Francisco Espinoza.

Four years removed from looking like one of the game’s best young starters, Miller is a big wild card at this point, but he’s making the minimum and still has two option years. item.content:encoded:
Dodgers acquired INF Royce Lewis from the Twins for RHP Bobby Miller and C Francisco Espinoza.

Imagine the electricity that would have surrounded a Lewis-for-Miller trade three years ago. However, since hitting .309/.373/.548 in 58 games as a rookie in 2023, Lewis has finished with OPSs of .747, .671 and .667. He’s also fallen down the defensive spectrum, though his introduction to second base last season might prove valuable to the Dodgers, who were looking for someone to share time with Tommy Edman. Edman will probably be pretty easily the better player of the two, but there’s still the chance that Lewis could recapture some of his former promise. If not, then the Dodgers can go to Alex Freeland. It’d probably take an injury to another infielder to make Lewis worth taking a chance on in mixed leagues next spring.

Minnesota moved Lewis before the deadline to decide whether to keep arbitration-eligible players.

In 2026, Lewis had 105 hits and 15 home runs in 125 games — the most he has played in a single season.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Projecting the Dodgers 2027 Starting Rotation: Who Replaces Tarik Skubal?
item.dc:creator: Noah Camras; Unknown
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are bringing back every member of their 2026 Opening Day starting rotation and all the starting pitchers they expected to help them through the season. And yet, they have a major hole in their rotation entering 2027. Tarik Skubal, who the Dodgers acquired ahead of the trade deadline, is a free agent, and is leaving a Cy-Young-shaped hole in LA's rotation. The Dodgers, of course, can bring him back, and will almost certainly be among the most aggressive teams pursuing him.
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are bringing back every member of their 2026 Opening Day starting rotation and all the starting pitchers they expected to help them through the season.
And yet, they have a major hole in their rotation entering 2027.
Tarik Skubal, who the Dodgers acquired ahead of the trade deadline, is a free agent, and is leaving a Cy-Young-shaped hole in LA's rotation.
The Dodgers, of course, can bring him back, and will almost certainly be among the most aggressive teams pursuing him.
If the Dodgers don't retain him, though, they still have plenty of internal options to replace him.
Here's a look at what the Dodgers' starting rotation could look like come Opening Day 2027 if Skubal leaves and the team decides against replacing him with an external option.
Dodgers' Likely 2027 Opening Day Rotation
- Yoshinobu Yamamoto, RHP
- Blake Snell, LHP
- Tyler Glasnow, RHP
- Roki Sasaki, RHP
- Justin Wrobleski, LHP
- Shohei Ohtani, RHP
Assuming health, these six pitchers should make up the Dodgers' six-man rotation to open the 2027 season.
Yamamoto is the surefire ace, while Snell and Glasnow, when healthy, are among the game's best pitchers.
Sasaki had a wire-to-wire 2026 season aside from a minor blister issue, while Wrobleski was a first-half All-Star before dealing with injury late in the season.
As for Ohtani, both he and the Dodgers are adamant about him being a two-way player in 2027. There's no reason to think he won't be in the team's Opening Day starting rotation next year.
The Depth Options
- Emmet Sheehan, RHP
- Gavin Stone, RHP
- Bobby Miller, RHP
- Jackson Ferris, LHP
Health isn't always on the Dodgers' side when it comes to starting pitching. It's also possible they delay Ohtani's two-way season in the hopes of him being healthier come the postseason.
If that's the case, the Dodgers still have plenty of potential depth options.
Sheehan made 23 starts last season and would likely be the first player to fill in. Stone had a 3.53 ERA across 25 starts in 2024 before undergoing shoulder surgery and missing the last two years.
Miller was a top pitching prospect for the Dodgers in 2023 but has struggled mightily over the last few years. He returned to MLB this year in a bullpen role, but could always be stretched out as a starter.
As for Ferris, he's currently a top pitching prospect for the Dodgers who needs to be added to the 40-man roster this offseason to avoid being eligible to be picked in the Rule 5 draft. He had a 5.12 ERA across 24 appearances (22 starts) in Triple-A Oklahoma City this past season.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA—After the 2023 season ended with a series sweep by their National League Western rival, the Arizona Diamondbacks, in the National League Championship Series, much of the blame fell on the starting rotation.
That was for good reason, as veteran left-hander Clayton Kershaw and right-handers Lance Lynn and Bobby Miller couldn’t power past the young, athletic D-Backs squad that rode that momentum to the Fall Classic.
That led Andrew Friedman and Co. to a massive problem to solve that winter, and he solved it by retooling the entire rotation, but first acquiring right-handed flamethrower Tyler Glasnow in a trade with Friedman’s old team, the Tampa Bay Rays.
But it wasn’t just a trade for Glasnow; Los Angeles also committed the time and money to keep their new arm beyond the 2024 season, inking him to a 5-year, $136 million extension despite his already lengthy injury history.
Still, the move paid off quickly for Los Angeles, as Glasnow set career highs in starts (22) and innings pitched (134.0). Still, a late-season elbow tendinitis injury shut the right-hander down just before October, and he missed the entire 2024 postseason run, which still ended with a World Series victory.
Glasnow would continue to battle the injury bug in 2025, this time making 18 starts after being shut down for much of the summer, pitching to a 3.19 ERA across 90 innings, but unlike 2024, Glasnow was able to make an impact in October.
In an October run defined by an elite starting rotation, Glasnow was dominant for Los Angeles, playing a key hybrid role and pitching critical innings in the NLDS against the Philadelphia Phillies and Toronto Blue Jays in the World Series while posting a 1.69 ERA over 21.1 innings.
Still, injuries were a concern, and in 2026 they were far from over: a lower back injury kept Glasnow out for most of the season, and unlike in 2025, the righty couldn’t replicate that October success, which ended in a Game Four defeat in the NLCS.
Now entering the 2027 offseason, Glasnow is set to make $32 million in his age-33 season with a looming $30 million club option for the 2028 season, a steep price for a starter that has averaged just over 99 innings in his stint with Los Angeles.
Could the Dodgers Move on From Glasnow to Make Room for a New Ace?
While money is just an object for the mighty Dodgers, they would still likely want more return on their investment, and it’s unlikely they’ll get that from Glasnow, who has still struggled to stay healthy.
For the most part, the 2027 starting rotation is set with the return of right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto, left-hander Blake Snell, and Shohei Ohtani, a formidable trio that could be even better with a healthy Glasnow but can be retooled without him.
Despite a second-half drop-off, left-hander Justin Worbleksi was a 2026 NL All-Star and was one of the team’s most dependable starters in the first half with Snell and Glasnow injured.
After a late-season demotion to Triple-A, right-hander Emmet Sheehan posted a sub-one ERA in September and is a prime candidate to rebound in 2027.
Then you have young Japanese right-hander Roki Sasaki, who is set to take another massive step in his development in 2027, where he’ll compete for a starting rotation spot after moving to the bullpen for Los Angeles in the postseason.
Whether it was a slight adjustment or enlargement of his glove to hold off tipping his pitches, Sasaki was exponentially better from July 17th until August 19th, when he went 2-0 with a 2.31 ERA and 1.17 WHIP across 35 innings, and continues to look excellent in relief upon his return from the IL in September.
Then you have the Dodgers’ biggest free agent this winter: two-time American League Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal, who, while he may have been a true deadline rental, could entertain a return to Los Angeles for the right price.
“It’s not easy for a guy to get traded in the middle of a season,” Friedman said, pointing to the adjustments required by a new city, clubhouse and routine.
“I can’t say enough good things about the impact that he made in such a short period of time,” Friedman said.
Skubal is expected to demand a contract likely at ten years at or around the $350-$400 million mark, and if he re-signs with the Dodgers, they’d likely want to untie their relationship for one of their arms earning over $30 million.
Despite his salary and injury history, many teams would kill for the chance to land Glasnow, especially for someone with No. 2 starter potential.
Still, Los Angeles would likely have to eat a majority of the salary or include premium prospects to get Glasnow’s deal off the books, but a team like the Texas Rangers or even the Los Angeles Angels makes sense.

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts ruled pitcher Blake Treinen out for the postseason after the right-hander suffered a shoulder injury warming up for a relief appearance in San Francisco.
Now, it sounds as if Roberts spoke prematurely.
Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said Saturday that Treinen's status for the postseason is "not decided firmly."
"It was clear for this round," Friedman said, "but we'll keep monitoring it as we go."
Friedman described the injury as "soreness" — a vague if much less ominous problem than the one Roberts suggested when Treinen was placed on the injured list after the Dodgers' Sept. 26 game against the Giants.
“I don't know if it was a complete blowout, but really unfortunate,” Roberts said at the time.
In 12 MLB seasons — the last six with the Dodgers — Treinen is 49-42 with a 2.94 ERA and 83 saves. Although he served as the Dodgers' closer only occasionally, he was a reliable source of strikeouts, low ERAs and some big postseason moments as the Dodgers captured three World Series championships this decade.
In 2024, Treinen saved three postseason games in three opportunities, allowing only three runs across nine October appearances. He was the winning pitcher in Game 5 of the 2024 World Series, when he threw 2.1 scoreless relief innings against the New York Yankees.
If the Dodgers need Treinen this month, it won't merely mean that he is healthy. It will mean somebody else — likely a couple somebodies — are not.
The Dodgers have enough quality and capable bullpen arms that they did not roster two pitchers who figured to be October mainstays (left-handers Justin Wrobleski and Jack Dreyer) in the National League Division Series. That decision was made in large part due to the Dodgers' opponent.
For Treinen to appear in a game this month, he'd have to prove more worthy of a roster spot than Tanner Scott, Alex Vesia, Brock Stewart, Roki Sasaki, Evan Phillips, Edgardo Henriquez, Edwin Diaz and Kris Bubic — plus Wrobleski and Dreyer.
Right-handers Bobby Miller and Emmet Sheehan have lockers and figure to be ready if called upon, too. Right-hander Will Klein finished the season on the injured list, like Treinen, but his throwing progression has put him in position to rejoin the roster if needed.
Treinen's possible availability is likely a mere footnote to the Dodgers' 2026 postseason run. Considering it sounded impossible a week ago, it's at least worth noting.

item.content:encoded:
SAN FRANCISCO – Well, enough of that – now on to the important stuff.
The Dodgers reached the end of the compulsory phase of their year, finishing the regular season with a 5-1 win in 10 innings against the San Francisco Giants on Sunday afternoon at Oracle Park.
The win was the Dodgers’ 100th of the season. It is the 12th time in franchise history that they have finished a season with 100 wins (including six of the past nine full seasons). None of the previous 100-win regular seasons were followed by a World Series championship.
The Dodgers will now take Monday off before getting together for four days of simulated games, live batting practice and whatever else they deem necessary to get ready for the opening of the postseason that will determine if they can become the first National League franchise to win three consecutive World Series championships.
Game 1 of their NL Division Series will be Saturday at Dodger Stadium against the winner of the Wild Card Series between the Atlanta Braves and Philadelphia Phillies. That best-of-three series begins Tuesday in Atlanta – and the Dodgers will be watching.
“There’s going to be some watch parties at the ballpark. I thought that was something that was really good,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of the bye week itinerary established in 2024. “You’re not playing in the Wild Card Series, but you’re watching it and you kind of get your juices going. There’s also a bonding piece that I think is important.
“I thought we did a good job of having enough live and game situations, simulating them. Our coaches are sort of revisiting what we did a couple years ago. If there’s things we want to improve on or what – it worked out well a couple years ago. A lot of it’s also contingent on how guys are feeling, making sure they get rested and reset.”
MLB’s easiest September schedule allowed the Dodgers to go into their bye week with positive momentum. They went 18-7 in the final month (including 6-0 against the Giants in the final 10 days). Only the San Diego Padres (19-6) had more wins in the month.
Those bye-week sim games essentially started this weekend at Oracle Park.
On Sunday, the Dodgers sent seven pitchers to the mound to get their work. They allowed one run on five hits — and survived giving up the potential game-deciding home run. Giants shortstop Christian Koss took Dodgers reliever Bobby Miller deep leading off the eighth inning — but replay review turned the home run into a foul ball.
Roki Sasaki made his third appearance out of the bullpen since returning from a blister and did nothing to undermine his status as perhaps the most important bullpen weapon the Dodgers will have this postseason. He struck out two of the three batters he faced in a 1-2-3 inning.
Over his three innings in relief, Sasaki has faced 11 batters and struck out six, allowing two hits in his first appearance and none since.
“I think the fastball’s better,” Roberts said, comparing the version of Sasaki the Dodgers got when they moved him to the bullpen last postseason. “I think the split’s better. It’s also nice that he’s already done it. Just in total, he’s just a better pitcher than he was last year and a lot more confident.”
Edwin Diaz continued to affirm his status as a rediscovered bullpen weapon with another 1-2-3 inning. And Roberts reported Edgardo Henriquez has been throwing bullpen sessions this weekend and will participate in the bye week workouts with the expectation that he will be ready to return from his lower back injury and be part of the Dodgers’ NLDS bullpen.
The Dodgers’ offense didn’t spark to life until the 10th inning when Alex Call doubled in the free runner then trotted home on a three-run home run by Andy Pages.

item.content:encoded:
For nine-plus innings, the Dodgers and Giants couldn’t buy a hit with a runner in scoring position, but in the tenth, the Dodgers broke through for a 5-1 win. Alex Call and Andy Pages recorded two-out hits, a double, and a three-run shot to give the Dodgers their first lead in this game and the only one they’d need.
Dodgers find their breakthrough in extras to beat the Giants
Making a habit out of squandering chances through nine innings, the Dodgers scored four in extras to beat the Giants
Before getting to that point of being tied in extras, Jack Dreyer did a reasonable job of keeping the Giants at bay as an opener, but a stolen base allowed the opportunity for just a pair of singles to open the scoring in the second. Shay Whitcomb singled and stole second, later driven in by Scott Bandura—his first RBI of the season, playing in just his 13th big league game. Bandura also tried to steal a base, but this time Dreyer was alert to the danger and picked him off.
Facing a traditional bullpen game with Carson Seymour completing just one inning to open this one, the Dodgers first threatened to score in the third, the inning marked by Tony Vitello’s ejection. With two on and a 2-2 count to Mookie Betts, a check swing in which he probably went around was called a no-swing. Vitello came out to argue what had already been a topic of frustration earlier in the game and was thrown out for the seventh time in his 2026. The Giants, however, got out of the jam, as Betts struck out on the next pitch, and Sam Hentges also punched out Freddie Freeman.
What the Dodgers offense couldn’t do in the third, it did in the following frame. Kyle Tucker got on to leadoff the inning thanks to a defensive error by the second baseman and moved to third on a Max Muncy double—his 27th of the season, setting a new career high in a single season. With two on and one out, Andy Pages evened the score with a sacrifice fly.
Through the following innings, the Dodgers kept threatening but never coming through, first with a Freddie Freeman hit with a man on being taken away by a great defensive play from Jonah Cox—somewhat redeeming himself for the error that contributed to the Dodgers’ first run. That, by the way, would be Freeman’s last action in the game, replaced after five by Kiké Hernández as Dave Roberts rotated key pieces.
In the sixth, Muncy nearly wrote another chapter in his book as a giant killer. But the deepest part of the park was just deep enough to keep him from a solo shot in a ball that would’ve gone out in 23 of 30 stadiums. Perhaps the biggest squandered chance, though, came in the seventh and eighth when the Dodgers first stranded a leadoff double by Tommy Edman with three straight groundouts—an inning later, after Muncy secured his third hit of the day, Andy Pages hit into an inning-ending double play with two on and one out.
The Dodgers’ pitching was the reason the offense kept getting these opportunities to take the lead. Justin Wrobleski was the first pitcher out of the bullpen for the Dodgers, but looking for an even distribution of workload, he only completed two scoreless innings in under 30 pitches. Roki Sasaki and Edwin Díaz combined to strike out three, each with a scoreless frame.
Although Wrobleski had a couple of scares, the Giants truly came back to threaten again in the seventh when Bobby Miller took the mound, but also without actually breaking through. With runners at the corners and no outs, Miller secured a strikeout, then lucked into Marcelo Mayer staying at third on a wild pitch quickly recovered by Hunter Feduccia, recorded another punchout, and finished off the inning with a groundout.
With both teams exhausting new ways of threatening without actually scoring, the Giants looked like they’d take the lead with a leadoff bomb in the eighth by Christian Koss. However, the call on the field of a home run was overturned when replay made it clear it was a foul ball, and the score remained 1-1 through nine innings.
Even in the tenth, it looked like the Dodgers were going to strand the ghost runner after their first two hitters were retired without him advancing to third, but Call came through, and an intentional walk later, Pages had the big hit of the game. With the four RBI he recorded in this game, Pages left Ohtani behind and isolated himself as the Dodgers’ RBI leader this season, with 85.
Sunday particulars
Home run: Andy Pages (23)
WP —Alex Vesia (3-1): 1 IP, 1 hit, 1 strikeout
LP —Duncan Davitt (0-1):1 IP, 2 hits, 4 runs, 3 earned runs, 1 walk
Up next
The Dodgers get a little under a week off before they get back on the field on Saturday at home. They’ll be playing host to the winner of the Wild Card round between the Braves and Phillies in game 1 of the NLDS. No starters have been announced for that series.
